pending_commit.commit_message: cryptohome: decouple cryptolib functions for SecureBlob/Blob Modify cryptolib to decouple Blobs and SecureBlobs under the rule that the hashing functions retain the base data type: instead of overloading the same function, create a separate function for Blob --> SecureBlob. This is in preparation for breaking the dependence between SecureBlob and Blob. This breaks function calls that implicitly convert into SecureBlob, therefore move the existing call functions into either SecureBlobs or use Sha*ToSecureBlob if the data is not moved/copied into another type. Move all Aes* functions to use SecureBlob for both ciphertext and plaintext: since most usages of Aes[En|De]crypt use SecureBlobs for both, this helps in decoupling mixed usage. Ideally, the ciphertext, once encrypted, should be a Blob: we revisit this once the dependence between SecureBlob and Blob is broken. BUG=chromium:728047 TEST=unittests pass. shill: fix default blackhole route creation This CL fixes a regression in the creation of default blackhole routes introduced by CL:1319984. The default blackhole routes should only be created when there is some UID or IP address to blackhole. CL:1319984 relies on a nullptr check on |IPConfig::Properties::blackholed_addrs| to determine if there is any IP address to blackhole. However, that's incorrect because |IPConfig::Properties::blackholed_addrs| is derived from |Device::blackholed_addrs_|, which is always not null even if there is no IP address to blackhole. As a minimal fix to address the regression, this CL explicitly checks if |IPConfig::Properties::blackholed_addrs| is empty or not. A follow-up CL should simplify the code path by avoiding nullptr for |IPConfig::Properties::blackholed_addrs|. shill: open stuff with _CLOEXEC We don't want any of these file descriptors to persist across exec(). While we might be able to get this (and we do try) with, e.g., ProcessManager::StartProcess() -> ProcessImpl::SetCloseUnusedFileDescriptors() and Minijail::CloseOpenFds(), it gets us extra sanity if we can just mark them when we open them. For unit tests: generally, the exact details of which SOCK_* args are used for the 2nd parameter are not extremely relevant to the tests. So rather than add SOCK_CLOEXEC to all of them, I tended toward choosing to make them "dont-care" args. For some cases, we really don't care about the socket details at all and are only ensuring that we don't need to open *any* new sockets, so in some cases, I make all the socket args don't care (so our test is simply "ensure no new Socket()s are opened"). In some cases, I also avoid repetitivity by specifying EXPECTed args in only one test case, while the other test cases become don't-care.
